title: Use case: stylized-concept. Edit the attached aircraft identity reference into a finished retro pixel-art title-screen SCENE for the MEGA65 vertical shooter Shooter65. The attached blue-silver player and olive bomber / gray-red armoured enemy are identity references only, not a layout to retain. Landscape 8:5 composition, intended final native resolution 320x200; render it as clean coarse pixel art on that exact logical grid, optionally enlarged 4x with square pixels. This is the scene layer: NO WORDS, NO LETTERS, no HUD, no border, no logos. Leave the top 44 logical pixels mostly dark indigo smoky sky as clear negative space for a large title to be added accurately; leave bottom 24 logical pixels plain very dark indigo for engine-written text. Main scene fills y=44..175. A large recognizable blue-silver PLAYER AIRCRAFT in a three-quarter overhead view sweeps up from lower-left toward upper-right, bright blue fuselage, silver wing tips, narrow warm orange cockpit highlight, twin orange exhaust; it fires several bright yellow-orange tracers toward a group of THREE large enemy aircraft on the upper-right, using the attached olive bomber and gray-red armoured aircraft designs, with one hit bursting into sparks. The enemy aircraft fire back toward the player. Below them stretches a HALF-DESTROYED CITY: broken towers, exposed floors, shattered rooftops and dark streets, some intact sections, small fires and smoke columns. Dramatic depth through overlapping silhouettes, but no realistic people, no gore. Authentic polished 16-bit-era pixel illustration with strong readable shapes, angular aircraft construction and hand-placed dithering. STRICT LIMITED PALETTE of 16 flat colors total: deep indigo/black, 3 blue-gray shadows, slate, silver-white, dark blue, electric cobalt and pale cyan for player, olive green shades for enemies, amber, orange and warm cream for fires. No anti-aliasing, no soft gradients, no blur, no painterly strokes. Keep the player design recognizable; do not substitute a modern realistic fighter. Large balanced graphic shapes must remain legible after native 320x200 conversion.
game_over: Use case: stylized-concept. Edit the attached aircraft identity reference into the scene layer for a MEGA65 Game Over illustration. Reference blue-silver player aircraft must remain recognizable even as a broken wreck. The attached reference board is identity guidance only; replace its layout completely. Landscape 8:5 composition, intended native resolution 320x200, coarse square-pixel art optionally enlarged 4x. NO WORDS, NO LETTERS, no HUD, no border, no logos. Leave the upper 48 logical pixels mostly dark indigo smoky sky with clear negative space for large GAME OVER text added later. Main subject across lower-middle: the blue-silver player has CRASHED on a fractured road among a destroyed CITY, one silver-tipped wing snapped and lying beside it, blue fuselage split open, dark smashed canopy with a small orange glint, bent tail and a few dying orange embers; it is clearly an aircraft wreck, no longer flying. Keep recognizable cobalt-blue fuselage and silver angular wings from the reference. Atmospheric ruined city skyline behind: bombed towers, exposed floors, hanging girders, rubble piles and broken streets; orange fires in two distant windows, dark smoke. Melancholy stillness and visual clarity, no human victims or gore. Strong silhouette of the wreck against cracked gray pavement, fires as small accents rather than a giant explosion. Authentic polished retro pixel-art cover illustration, exactly 16 flat colors total, shared family of deep indigo, slate blue-gray, silver, cobalt, cyan, dark olive, amber/orange/cream. No antialiasing, blur, smooth gradients or photographic detail; prefer angular 1-3 native pixel clusters and restrained ordered dithering. Composition should preserve a readable wreck in a small game-over banner crop as well as the full 320x200 image.
